title: Dedicated/VPC telemetry fanout and tenant isolation guardrails
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a robust telemetry fanout and per-tenant isolation layer for Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket covers:collector deployment options (sidecar vs centralized), per-tenant pipeline separation, enforced metadata tagging for traces/logs/metrics, tenant-level retention & cost guardrails, mutual-TLS and routing policies for VPC collectors, and an operational playbook for on-prem air-gapped installs. Goal: allow tenant telemetry to be routed or held in isolation without mixing telemetry streams while preserving low-latency trace hooks for inference-critical paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deployable collector topology documented for sidecar and central modes with config examples.
2) Telemetry fanout implemented so tenant A and B never share pipeline state or secrets (proof: e2e test showing pipeline isolation).
3) Tracing hooks available with <4ms added P95 latency on inference path under 200 RPS synthetic load.
4) mTLS + tenant ACLs validated via automated integration tests.
5) Runbook for offline on-prem installs and upgrade notes added to confluence and Ops repo.
tasks: Draft design doc and topology diagrams (sidecar vs central) - initial draft complete
Implement collector routing plugin that attaches tenant id and writes to tenant namespaces
Add server-side pipeline isolation (separate Kafka topics / file sinks / S3 prefixes) support
Instrument inference runtime with lightweight trace hooks and sampling config
Add automated e2e tests for isolation and latency (CI jobs for dedicated/private)
Document security model: mTLS, KMS integration for pipeline credentials
Create Ops runbook for on-prem upgrade/rollback with telemetry fallback steps
comments: 2025-01-10 - Ava Chen: Spiked sidecar vs central collector tradeoffs. Sidecar gives tenant network isolation but increases resource footprint on inference nodes. Central collector reduces overhead but needs stronger per-tenant ACLs and namespace-level enforcement.

2025-01-16 - Ravi Kapoor: PoC for trace hook added. Hook attaches tenant_id, request_id, model_version at <3ms median. P95 currently around 12ms under synthetic burst; needs optimization (KV cache hotpath).
2025-01-21 - Design feedback (Maya Patel): Prefer configurable defaults for retention and sampling per customer; avoid hard-coded tiers. UX will expose per-customer policy in Console later.
2025-01-28 - Security review (Jonah Lee): Require mTLS for any collector connection into customer VPCs. Also flagged KMS usage for credential rotating; added to scope.
2025-02-03 - Infra note (Luis Martinez): Centralized collector model needs tenant-aware resource quotas in K8s to prevent noisy-neighbor. Added resourceQuota patterns to the implementation plan.

2025-02-10 - QA (Priya N.): Added integration test that replays 10k traces across 50 tenants for isolation verification; found a bug where header normalization stripped tenant X- header for legacy clients — patch linked below.
notes: Decisions: 1) Default deployment for Dedicated will be central collector with optional per-node sidecar for high-security tenants. 2) We will implement tenant namespaces in the pipeline layer using tenant_id claim and signed metadata. 3) Sampling will be configurable per-tenant; default retention bands documented. Performance mitigations include async batching of non-critical logs and prioritized path for trace spans.
risks: 1) On-prem air-gapped environments may lack metrics backends (e.g., SaaS S3); plan includes local file sink + periodic secure export. 2) Noisy tenant could still impact centralized collector CPU without strict K8s quotas. 3) Backwards compatibility for older SDKs that don't send tenant headers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for routing plugin, integration tests with a 3-node cluster simulating 100 tenants, e2e perf benchmark to validate <4ms added latency P95 for trace hooks. CI job will run isolation test suite on feature branches. Manual on-prem validation steps documented in runbook.
implementation_notes: Prototype code in collector repo uses a plugin shape so downstream sinks (kafka/s3/file) get a tenant_prefix parameter. We will use mTLS client certs for collector-to-backend auth and KMS-wrapped credentials for artifacts. Config examples include helm values for central and sidecar modes.
next_steps: 1) Merge collector routing plugin PR and enable smoke tests on staging. 2) Ramp sampling config to reduce P95. 3) Coordinate with Console team to surface per-tenant telemetry settings. 4) Schedule on-prem validation with 2 pilot customers.
